documents.title: Guidance for Using Generative AI in Teaching & Learning at Mines: Guidance for Faculty
documents.date_or_term: undated (current page; original guidelines released August 2023)
documents.summary: University-wide guidance from the Provost's office telling faculty that Mines has no uniform rule: instructors may fully integrate or ban genAI as long as they explain the choice. It offers a syllabus statement template, transparency practices, assessment redesign ideas, advice against relying on AI detectors, and rules for privacy and instructor AI use.
documents.stance_why: The document says 'We aren’t looking for a single, uniform approach' and that faculty may 'fully integrate genAI or completely ban it', pointing to a syllabus statement 'to permit or prohibit genAI use'. It sets no default itself and hands the decision to instructors, so delegates.

units.why: States the university's overall stance as no single rule: 'the only truly "forbidden" stance on AI is the denial of its impact', so integrating or banning is up to the faculty member. Chosen P04 (instructor decides) over P02 because neither use nor ban is the default.
